transcript.content: I've been experiencing these intense mood swings where I feel incredibly high and full of energy, but then I suddenly become extremely irritable and angry at the smallest things. It's getting really hard to manage, and that's mainly why I'm here today.
During these episodes of feeling incredibly high or extremely irritable, have you ever experienced any break from reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there?

No, I've never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, and I've never felt like I lost touch with reality. It's just my mood and energy that feel completely out of control.
Have you ever had a manic episode that lasted at least 7 days, or was so severe that you needed to be hospitalized, and were you unable to function in your daily life during these episodes?

No, I've never been hospitalized or found myself completely unable to function. Instead, I had a period of about 11 months where I felt the opposite—extremely energetic, constantly on the go, and highly active both at work and socially, even though my mood was elevated and very irritable.

During those 11 months, did you experience any periods of at least 4 consecutive days where you felt elevated or irritable, and had increased energy, but were still able to function in your daily life and didn't necessarily need to be hospitalized?

Yes, definitely. During those 11 months, I had several periods lasting much longer than four days where my energy was overflowing and I felt extremely elevated or irritable. Even though I was hyperactive and constantly on the go, I was still able to get through my daily routine and never needed to be hospitalized.

Have you experienced any major depressive episodes, lasting at least two weeks, where you felt persistently sad, empty, or lost interest in activities you once enjoyed, in addition to these periods of elevated mood and energy?

Yes, I definitely have. I went through a very long period of about a year and two months where I felt constantly depressed, sad, and completely empty inside. During that time, I lost all interest in the activities I used to enjoy and just couldn't bring myself to care about anything.

Did these periods of elevated mood and energy occur before, after, or both before and after the major depressive episode you described, and were there any noticeable patterns or triggers to these mood shifts?

I'm not really sure about the exact order of when they happened or what triggers them. I just know that the high-energy period lasted for about 11 months, while the depressed period went on for about a year and two months.

Can you try to recall if the major depressive episode and the high-energy period ever overlapped, or if one clearly started after the other had ended, to help clarify the pattern of your mood episodes?
I'm not quite sure about the exact timing or whether those two periods overlapped. It is just really difficult for me to recall the precise sequence of when they started and ended.
During these episodes of feeling incredibly high or extremely irritable, have you ever experienced any break from reality, such as hearing voices or seeing things that aren't there?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I don't hear voices or see things that aren't there, even when my mood is at its most extreme.

Can you distinguish between the periods of elevated mood where you felt extremely energetic and those where you felt extremely irritable, and did either of these types of episodes significantly impact your daily life or relationships?

They aren't really separate, as my mood shifts unpredictably between feeling euphoric and full of energy to suddenly becoming highly irritable. These episodes definitely impact my life because when I'm highly energetic, I take on way too much work and become overly social. This ends up being exhausting and really disruptive to my daily routine and relationships.

How have these episodes of elevated mood and energy, as well as the depressive episodes, affected your overall functioning, relationships, and daily life, and are you currently experiencing any distress or impairment due to these symptoms?

These alternating episodes have caused huge disruptions in my life, as I'd become overly social and take on too many work projects during my high-energy phases. In contrast, during my depressive periods, I completely withdrew from everyone, lost all motivation to work, and struggled with severe sleep disturbances. This constant back-and-forth has made it incredibly difficult to maintain a stable daily routine and has caused me a lot of distress.
